speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To understand the timeline and nature of these symptoms, can you tell me when these problems first started and if they are getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hashimoto's Encephalopathy (Steroid-responsive Encephalopathy associated with Autoimmune Thyroiditis)

The patient's 6-month history of progressive cognitive decline, paranoia, and agitation preceding the acute 1-week onset of gait ataxia and right leg weakness suggests a subacute autoimmune encephalopathy. I need to confirm thyroid function and rule out paraneoplastic syndromes. REQUEST TEST: TSH, Free T4, Anti-Thyroid Antibodies (TPO, Tg, Anti-TTG); REQUEST TEST: CSF Analysis; REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.
